inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (operating company route, SKILL.md table row 2 — cyclical non-US operating company; section 7 adaptations applied). FRESH BUILD — no prior DCF. FY0 anchor is FY2026E (12 months to 30 Sep 2026, guided): revenue ~NZ$191m (H1 actual $100.3m + est. winter H2 ~$91m; ~6,000t at ~NZ$32/kg), Pro-Forma EBITDA guidance $30-34m. LEASES (IFRS 16, treatment B): lease principal (~NZ$1.9m/yr, ~1% of revenue) expensed inside the EBITDA margin path; lease liabilities ($9.2m) EXCLUDED from net debt — net debt is borrowings $1.934m minus cash $40.155m = -$38.221m (Mar-2026). INTEREST INCOME (~$0.9m/yr) stripped: net cash ($38.2m) far exceeds the FCF base. SBC ~$0.14m/yr (0.07% of revenue) — near-SBC-zero market; house/street band collapses (spread ~NZ$0.002/share), band_position=null. last_fcf $2.49m = FY2026E reported-basis FCF est. $5.40m − SBC $0.14m − interest income $0.87m − lease principal $1.90m; the projections are component-built, not grown off last_fcf. GAAP vs PRO-FORMA WARNING: management guides on Pro-Forma Operating EBITDA which strips IAS 41 biological-asset fair-value swings; it has diverged materially from GAAP (H1 FY2026: GAAP EBITDA $23.95m vs Pro-Forma $17.23m; prior 6mo GAAP -$25.1m vs Pro-Forma +$5.7m). This model uses the pro-forma level as the cash-generative anchor and mid-cycle GAAP-consistent margins thereafter; guidance treated as directional only. FUNDING: full-scale Blue Endeavour (~10,000t, ~$350m revenue ambition) is NOT in any scenario's explicit years; bull carries only partial phased scale-up funded within the modelled capex envelope — a full build-out would likely require new equity (dilution) or debt not modelled here.

assumptions.wacc_rationale: Built from NZD flows: NZ 10yr govt ~4.5% + NZX small-cap ERP ~7% -> ~11.5% standard NZ small-cap base. Structural premiums, each documented: +1.75% extreme biological/climate cyclicality beyond what three discrete scenarios capture (GAAP EBITDA swung -$15.6m to +$47.0m within five years; the continuous/fat-tail version of the mortality risk, distinct from the discrete recurrence path carried in the bear scenario); +2.0% small-cap illiquidity (mkt cap ~NZ$129m, thin float, Oregon Group ~40% register concentration); +1.25% single-species/single-region concentration (one fish, one sound, no diversification); +1.0% resource-consent/regulatory single-point-of-failure (business exists only by consents to 2044-2057). Total 17.5%, applied identically to all three scenarios (risk charged once: discrete mortality-recurrence path lives in the bear scenario WEIGHT, structural/continuous risk lives in WACC; no per-scenario WACC differences).
assumptions.terminal_cap_rationale: 12x FCF cap (low end of the cyclical 12-15x band) for a capacity-constrained biological producer; Gordon at 17.5%/2.0% implies 6.6x and binds in all scenarios, well under the cap

base.narrative: BASE: the guided inshore ramp mostly delivers, with a haircut for NZK's history of missed biological forecasts — wellboat-enabled harvest growth toward ~7,200t (FY27 guide 7,200-7,600t) then ~8,000t+ (FY28 guide 8,500-9,100t, haircut), revenue decelerating from +15% to 2% terminal. Post-lease EBITDA margin recovers from 15.0% (FY27, cost inflation persisting per guidance) to a 17.0% mid-cycle level — deliberately below FY2024's 25% GAAP peak and above FY2025-Jan's 12.5%. Capex stays elevated (9.5% of revenue) through the Blue Endeavour pilot/RAS phase then fades to 5% maintenance. Working capital consumes 20% of each revenue increment (biomass build — growing fish is inventory). Cash tax ramps 18%->28% NZ statutory by year 3. No mortality catastrophe, no full-scale Blue Endeavour.

bull.narrative: BULL: the recovery is structural, not a good season — thermotolerant breeding, summer diet and the wellboat hold mortality down; the guided ramp to ~9,000t delivers in full, and the Blue Endeavour PILOT succeeds, supporting a phased partial commercial scale-up (roughly half-scale by year 10, NOT the full 10,000t/~$350m ambition, which would need funding beyond the modelled envelope). Revenue compounds 17% tapering to 4%; premium King-salmon pricing power lifts post-lease margins to 19%; capex runs at 10% of revenue for five years to build it. Same tax ramp and WACC as base.

bear.narrative: BEAR: a warm-summer mortality event recurs in FY2028 (year 2) — a real, recent, observed outcome (FY2022: up to ~42% mortality at warm sites, -$73.2m NPAT), not a tail fantasy. Revenue drops 18%, post-lease EBITDA margin collapses to ~1% in the event year and recovers only to a 14% mid-cycle (structurally warmer Sounds), harvest never reaches the FY28 guide. Blue Endeavour pilot disappoints and full scale-up is shelved (capex fades to maintenance). Destocking returns some working capital cash in the down year (as in FY2025-Jan). Tax losses suppress cash tax through the recovery. The company survives on its $38m net cash without another rights issue — a second capital raise on crisis terms is the residual risk BELOW this case.

entry_price.note: The 15% hurdle is BELOW the 17.5% WACC, so hurdle entry prices sit ABOVE intrinsic value (a buyer content with 15% can pay more than the 17.5%-required-return fair value). The binding buy-below price is therefore the probability-weighted IV (NZ$0.234), not the weighted hurdle entry price (NZ$0.264). Bear-case entry NZ$0.164 vs price NZ$0.24: a 15% return from today requires avoiding the mortality-recurrence path.

required_return_table.note: Today's NZ$0.24 against the base-case path implies a required return of ~18.5% — above the model's own 17.5% WACC. The market is pricing NZK at a distressed-cyclical discount rate, consistent with the post-crisis multiple regime (P/B 0.66-0.83x since FY2023).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default. Bear DOUBLED to 30%: mortality recurrence is an observed, recent outcome (FY2022) driven by a structural warming trend, and the current recovery is only 1-2 good biological seasons old in a company with a long record of missed forecasts. Bull CUT to 20%: it requires several independent things to go right — sustained biological performance, full delivery of a harvest ramp NZK has historically missed, AND a world-first open-ocean system (already ~1 year late) succeeding at pilot then scaling. Base 50%: the guided, wellboat-enabled inshore ramp with a haircut.
probability_weighted.band_note: Near-SBC-zero company (SBC ~0.07% of revenue): house and street IVs differ by ~NZ$0.002/share, so the accounting-regime band collapses and band_position is null rather than a degenerate figure.

sanity_check.method: Implied base-case multiples vs ~10y of own trading history. Monthly Yahoo closes; pre-Apr-2022 prices de-adjusted by the ~0.50 TERP factor Yahoo applied for the 2022 rights issue (verified against two anchors: Oct-2016 IPO at NZ$1.12 shows as 0.585; Feb/Mar-2019 real peak ~NZ$2.95 shows as 1.473). FY-end months tracked through BOTH balance-date changes: June for FY2016-FY2020, January for FY2022-FY2025-Jan, September thereafter. Stub periods (FY2021-7mo, FY2025-8mo) skipped entirely; FY2022 kept in the table but EXCLUDED from averages (mortality crisis). FY2016 skipped (pre-IPO, no market price). P/E unstable across loss years; P/B and EV/EBITDA are the primary anchors, as NZK pays no dividend.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trips. Base-case upside +4.8% is far below the 100% auto-trip threshold despite the price sitting in the upper half of its 52-week range (0.189-0.255). Implied base P/B 0.64x vs 1.27x historical average (ex-crisis) and implied EV/EBITDA ~3.0-3.2x vs 7.37x average — the model prices NZK BELOW its own history, not above. Context: the market itself has traded in two regimes — pre-crisis P/B 1.37-2.35x, post-crisis (FY2023-FY2025) 0.66-0.83x and EV/EBITDA 3.0-8.8x. The model's implied multiples sit at the bottom of the POST-crisis regime, i.e. the valuation embeds the market's current risk pricing rather than assuming a re-rate back to pre-crisis multiples. The gap between the two regimes (~2x) is the price of proving the biological recovery is structural.

valuation_philosophy.summary: NZK is valued as a severely cyclical biological producer, not a compounder. The engine is the house owner-FCF DCF, but every lever is set for cyclicality: (1) mid-cycle margins, never the recovery half — H1 FY2026's swing to +$13.8m NPAT follows a -$20.8m half and sits between a -$73m crisis and a +$28m peak, so the base margin (17% post-lease) deliberately sits well below the FY2024 peak; (2) a high-teens WACC (17.5%) carrying documented structural premiums for biology/climate, illiquidity, concentration and consent dependence; (3) a bear case that is an observed outcome — the FY2022 mortality event rerun — weighted at a full 30%; (4) Blue Endeavour treated as an option: the base case carries only the wellboat-enabled inshore ramp (haircut), the bull carries a partial phased scale-up, and the full ~10,000t/~$350m ambition appears in NO scenario's explicit years because it is unbuilt, capital-hungry and already late; (5) terminal growth 2.0% for a capacity-constrained producer, TV capped at 12x FCF (Gordon binds at 6.6x anyway); (6) GAAP-consistent cash economics with the pro-forma/GAAP divergence flagged rather than papered over. The result — weighted IV NZ$0.234 vs price NZ$0.24 — says the market is pricing NZK roughly fairly for its risk: the upside case is real but so is the recurrence risk, and neither dominates at this price.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_the_view: UP: two more clean biological years (FY27 harvest within guide), Blue Endeavour pilot fish surviving to harvest at commercial cost, or a funded path to scale without dilution — each would justify cutting the bear weight toward 15-20% and lifting IV toward the bull case. DOWN: any summer mortality spike, an FY27 guidance miss, or an equity raise for Blue Endeavour at a discount — the bear path activating.
